target_customer: Small healthcare practices, first dental and optometry offices, later other appointment-based small businesses, that pay a monthly subscription
problem: Small practices ran phones, patient reminders, texting and payments on disconnected tools, so front desks lacked patient context when a call arrived and missed revenue.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per location with bundled VoIP phones, texting, reminders and payments
product_category: Customer communication and payments platform for small practices

founders.name: Brandon Rodman
previous_startups: Recall Solutions (patient recall for dental offices, became Weave)
founders.background_notes: Roy Banks later became CEO, per the 2021 S-1 coverage.

founders.name: Clint Berry
founders.background_notes: Listed as CTO on the YC page.

competitors.name: Henry Schein Dental and Patterson Dental
competitors.what: Dominant dental suppliers selling front office software and services
competitors.traction_then: Dominant incumbents of the dental front office market

technical_complexity.rationale: Routing office phone calls through a cloud PBX and integrating caller lookup with practice management software was standard VoIP plus integrations, with the hard part being reliability and many software integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Phones and integrations created some switching costs once installed, but VoIP and reminders were copyable and incumbents sold adjacent tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge in the early years; Weave grew to an IPO in 2021 and was then reported sold to Francisco Partners in 2026.

market_need_then: Dental offices were reported to lose time on phones and manual patient follow up; TechCrunch coverage at the February 2014 launch reported over 200 paying customers already.

branding.name_origin: Not explained by a source; the company began as Recall Solutions and became Weave, with sources disagreeing on the date of the rename.
branding.domain_note: Uses getweave.com, a prefix domain, rather than weave.com.

identity.logo: Updated logo meant to convey unity and possibility, per the company
identity.visual_style: Clean, modern software look with a published brand site
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, upbeat, direct, short taglines focused on efficiency and patient care

rebrands.why: Sources conflict on whether the rename was 2010 or 2015; reason not stated

brand_strength.rationale: A solid vertical SaaS brand with a brand guidelines site and an NYSE listing, but no evidence of fan community, memes or merch, and the name is shared with many other companies.

outcome_analysis: Weave found early demand among dental offices by bundling phones with patient context, reached over 200 paying customers by its 2014 launch, raised growth rounds led by Tiger Global at a reported 970 million dollar valuation in 2019, and listed on the NYSE in November 2021 below its range. Later coverage reports a roughly 650 million dollar take private by Francisco Partners in 2026, which is below the IPO era valuation, so the outcome was a public company that stalled in value.
notes: Seed to Series B amounts not verified; total raised before IPO ranges from about 150 to 193 million across sources. Founding year 2008 (as Recall Solutions) versus 2011 conflicts. The 2026 Francisco Partners take private is reported by secondary outlets with conflicting dates and the directory still lists Public. Competition list is thin because dated 2014 sources named only the dental suppliers.
